title: Writing a laboratory report
competency: Write a clear laboratory report with its parts in the right order.

keywords.def: A place where science experiments are done. It builds observation skills, skill with apparatus and independent thinking.
A written account of the results of an experiment, written precisely and clearly.
What you want to find out or show in an experiment.
The steps you followed, in order.
What you saw and measured while you worked.
A short answer to your objective.

en.text: The laboratory is where science experiments are done. It builds your observation, your skill with apparatus and your independent thinking. A laboratory report is a written account of the results of an experiment. Write it precisely and clearly, with good grammar and punctuation.

am.text: ቤተ ሙከራ የሳይንስ ሙከራዎች የሚደረጉበት ቦታ ነው። የቤተ ሙከራ ሪፖርት የሙከራ ውጤቶች የጽሑፍ መግለጫ ነው። በትክክል፣ በግልጽ እና በጥሩ ሰዋስው መጻፍ አለበት።

screens.title: A friend was absent
screens.text: Your class in Bahir Dar tested which cloth dries fastest. Your friend Liya was absent that day.
screens.ask: What is the best way for Liya to learn what you did and found?
opts: Read a clear written report of the experiment
screens.after: Scientists write reports for this reason. Read on.

ideas.name: Parts of a laboratory report, in order

en.text: Every report has the same parts, in order. Date, title, objective, theory, materials, chemicals, procedure, observation, result, discussion, conclusion. First you say what you planned. Then what you did and saw. Last, what it means.

screens.title: The parts of a report
paras: Every report must include these parts, in this order.
table: The day you did the experiment.
A short name for the experiment.
What you want to find out or show.
The science ideas behind the experiment.
The apparatus and equipment you used.
The steps you followed, in order.
What you saw and measured while you worked.
The outcome of the experiment, such as a table of readings.
What the results mean and why they came out that way.
A short answer to your objective.

screens.title: Key parts
defs: What you want to find out or show.
The steps you followed, in order.
What you saw and measured while you worked.
A short answer to your objective.

screens.title: Where do readings go?
screens.ask: In which part of a report do you write what you saw and measured?
screens.why: Observations are what you saw and measured during the experiment.
screens.clue: Look at the "What it holds" column of the table.

screens.title: Put the parts in order
screens.text: Put these parts of a laboratory report in order.
screens.why: A report goes from what you planned, to what you did and saw, to what you decided.
screens.clue: Start with when and what. End with your answer to the objective.
screens.worked: Date → Title → Objective → Materials → Procedure → Observation → Result → Conclusion.

screens.title: The last part
screens.ask: The part that gives a short answer to your objective is the ___.
screens.why: The conclusion is a short answer to your objective. It comes last.
screens.clue: It is the last of the eleven parts.

screens.title: Liya's list
screens.text: Liya writes: "beaker, thermometer, Bunsen burner, tongs".
screens.ask: Which part of her report is this?
screens.why: The materials part lists the apparatus and equipment you used.
screens.clue: Which part lists apparatus and equipment?

items.ask: 1. Which one is NOT allowed in a science laboratory?
opts: Knowing the hazards of the materials being used
Reading the labels on reagent bottles carefully
Not using laboratory glassware for eating or drinking
Wearing any type of clothes and shoes
items.ans: Wearing any type of clothes and shoes
items.why: You must dress properly for the lab.
items.clue: Three of these are good habits. Which one breaks a rule about dress?

items.ask: 2. Which laboratory tool is used for approximate measurement of the volume of liquids?
items.why: A measuring (graduated) cylinder has a volume scale.
items.clue: Which tool has a millilitre (ml) scale?

items.ask: 3. Which laboratory equipment is classed as measuring equipment?
items.clue: Which one gives you a number, like a mass?

items.ask: Part II, 4. Which of these is NOT a laboratory safety rule?

test.text: Put these parts of a laboratory report in order.
test.why: A report goes from what you planned, to what you did and saw, to what you decided.

test.ask: A laboratory report explains what you did, what you learnt and what the ___ mean.
test.why: A report ends by explaining what the results show.

test.text: In which part do you list the steps you followed?
test.why: The procedure is the steps you followed, in order.

notes.text: The book lists only the names of the eleven report parts. The short description of each part is added to help.

The "Unit 1 Review exercise" entry holds Review exercise Parts I–III (book pages 16–19). Parts IV (fill in the blanks) and V (short answers) are not included. Part III is a matching task in the book, kept here as one multiple-choice item per field, as in the source.

Exercise 1.3 Q2 asks for "approximate" volume and the book answer is the measuring cylinder, while the 1.2.1 correction says a beaker gives approximate volume and a cylinder a more accurate one. The book answer is kept; teacher to check the wording.
